questions.q: The rule of thirds suggests you place key features where?
options: Along lines that divide the image into thirds or at their intersections
In the exact centre of the image
Around the edges of the frame
questions.explain: The rule of thirds divides the picture into a 3x3 grid and places focal points on the lines or intersections.

questions.q: What does adding white to a colour create?
questions.explain: Adding white to a colour produces a tint (a lighter version), while adding black produces a shade.

questions.q: In a mono-print, how many prints can usually be taken from one inking?
questions.explain: A mono-print produces a single, unique image, unlike editions made from a fixed block or plate.
The 'B' scale denotes softer, darker pencils, so 6B is much softer and darker than an H grade.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a sketchbook in GCSE Art?
options: To record ideas and show development of work
questions.explain: A sketchbook records observations, experiments and the development of ideas towards a final piece.

questions.q: How are complementary colours defined on the colour wheel?
options: Colours that sit next to each other
Different tones of the same hue
Colours that sit directly opposite each other
questions.explain: Complementary colours are positioned opposite one another on the colour wheel, such as red and green.

options: Pouring liquid material into a mould to set into shape
questions.explain: Casting pours a liquid such as molten metal or plaster into a mould, where it hardens into the form.

questions.q: Which medium is a soft, powdery stick available in soft (chalk) or oil form?
questions.explain: Pastels are sticks of pigment, made as soft chalk pastels or richer oil pastels.

questions.q: What does 'tone' refer to in the formal elements?
options: The lightness or darkness of an area
questions.explain: Tone describes how light or dark an area is, helping to create the illusion of form.

options: Thick paint applied with a knife
A thin, transparent layer of diluted paint
questions.explain: A wash is a thin, transparent layer of watercolour spread over an area to build colour gradually.

questions.q: Which group are considered warm colours?
questions.explain: Reds, oranges and yellows are warm colours, while blues, greens and violets are cool.

questions.q: Two-point perspective uses how many vanishing points?
questions.explain: Two-point perspective uses two vanishing points on the horizon, typically for objects seen at a corner.
